agent-coordination.purpose: Everything between handle holders: asks (tag one handle), announcements (tag some, or none for all), their threads.
agent-coordination.routed_by: each sender: `research msg` rings the addressed handles' inbox threads (routes.d), and every holder subscribes to its own inbox thread; no agent forwards

agent-alerts.purpose: Machine alerts. Every top-level post is addressed to the subscribers.

ask-daniel.purpose: Everything that needs Daniel: one question per card (blocking or default), each linking its page in the Asks for Daniel Notion database; only Daniel (U0BEN96ES8Y) decides.

ask-the-team.purpose: Daniel's questions to the team, typed by him or posted by his Claude app through Slack's connector; top routes each one and answers in its thread, and lanes top asks may reply there with --channel-id.

resource-accounting.purpose: Collaborators' questions on compute, memory and network accounting and the GPU model they rest on.

handles.remit: Machines and task infra: utilization, the scheduler, buying compute, alerts, and one API for agents' jobs.
examples: Which machines do we have right now, and what is each one busy with?
I want to run a long job on a GPU tonight. Where can it go, and how do I start it?
My run failed or was killed. Why, and where are its logs?
How much are our machines costing per day, and when does each one shut down?
Can I get access to a node, or more disk or memory for my job?

handles.remit: C-Flock, its guarantees (recursion's knowledge soundness, the ZK server's zero knowledge), SPOT, red team, proof-system sweeps.
handles.charter: PRF-282 and proofs' goals on the Goals page: proofs/recursion-knowledge-sound, proofs/zero-knowledge, proofs/zero-knowledge-any-worker
examples: What exactly have you proved about the proof system, and what do you still assume?
If a server cheats on only a small part of its work, how likely is a sampled check to catch it?
Does checking a proof reveal anything about the model's weights or the user's data?
Who checks the verifier? What if the verifier program itself has a bug?
Can one proof vouch for many others, so checking stays cheap at datacenter scale?

handles.remit: Circuits of real workloads: each served model's circuit, its capture and commitments, the primitives' Definitions and circuit-check.
examples: How do you turn a model like GLM or DeepSeek into a circuit, and how big is that circuit?
How many gates does one decoding step of a large model take, and which parts of the model dominate?
How do you know the circuit computes exactly what the GPU kernel actually computed, bit for bit?
How much slower is serving a model when you record and commit everything it computes?
Which models and batch sizes have a finished, published circuit record so far?

handles.remit: PoUW, its schemes and runs; served-path compute accounting (H200 share, credit in AND gates); its interfaces with circuits, kernels, vllm.
examples: How do you prove a GPU actually did the matrix multiplies it claims, rather than something cheaper?
What stops a datacenter from counting work done by its host CPU or a spare GPU as the audited GPU's work?
Where do the peak-throughput numbers for H200, B200 and RTX PRO 6000 come from, and how are they checked?
What exactly is credited as useful work when serving an LLM, and what isn't?
How much overhead does the proof of useful work add to inference, and how is it measured?

handles.remit: PoUW's lead scheme and Lean statements, weights hardened against matmul shortcuts, silicon logging and its forcing margin, machine model.
Memory accounting: PoUS, PoUB (the bandwidth audits) and secure erasure, the memory challenger, their Lean and their runs.
examples: How do you know the weights were actually held in GPU memory the whole time, and not reloaded from disk when you checked?
What stops a node from rebuilding the blocks you ask for on the fly instead of storing them?
How fast can the node pull data in from its disks or the network, and how does that change the memory number?
When a server is wiped, how do you prove nothing of the old contents survived?
What do the 19% memory and 75% bandwidth figures mean, and what are they assuming about the hardware?

handles.remit: Network accounting: the network certifier (verity/protocols/certifier) and its timing-channel proofs.
examples: How do you stop a GPU node from secretly sending data out over the network?
What does the network certifier record about each link, and who has to trust it?
How many bits could a cheating machine leak just through when it sends packets?
If two machines exchange model activations, how do you check the traffic is only what the model computes?
What happens to the audit if a certifier goes down or a node is under maintenance?

handles.remit: The live console and docs site: panels, formats, frontends, and what agents publish to them.
Daniel's dashboards on the console: the Goals page and live plots of running experiments. Asks wait until Daniel opens it; nothing wakes it.
examples: How do I put my goals on Daniel's Goals page?
How do I publish a live plot of my runs to the console?

handles.remit: Open PRs: shepherds each to a passing check and into the merge trains.
handles.charter: Daniel, 2026-10-01 10:56 AM PDT (leads get handles); named ci, not pr-captain (Daniel, 1:07 PM PDT)
examples: When will my pull request land on main, and what is it waiting for?
Why did my PR get taken out of the merge queue?
A check failed on my change but I don't think I broke it. Can you look?
How do I run the same checks locally before I mark my PR ready?
Why is landing on main slow right now, and is it getting faster?

handles.remit: Lean: the Lean audit and its tooling; a change to a Lean guarantee DMs Daniel when it lands.
examples: How do I know the Lean proofs actually check, with no sorry or extra axioms?
What does a security guarantee in Lean assume, and where is that written down?
My Lean build or proof check runs out of memory or takes hours. What should I do?
I changed a Lean definition and the check says a record changed. What do I run?
Can I trust a proof that imports Mathlib or ArkLib, and how are those checked?

handles.remit: Agent-to-agent messages: research msg, the names directory, routing, and its traffic.
examples: Who should I ask about something, and how do I reach them here?
My question got no answer. Who saw it, and what happens next?
How do I get my own chat channel, or add someone to it?

handles.remit: Top-level: Daniel's coordinator across every lead.
The vLLM integration: what the served model runs under verification, and its hookup to the protocols.
handles.charter: Daniel, 2026-10-13 (a new slice, in architecture's rollout)
examples: How do you check that a model served with vLLM computed exactly what it claims to?
Does verification slow down serving, and by how much?
Which models and quantizations (like int8 Llama) can you serve under verification today?
How do you prove the GPUs actually held the model's weights in memory while serving?
What changes when a model runs across several GPUs (tensor parallel)?

handles.remit: Benchmarks: the overhead and throughput measurements across proof systems, and the tables rendered from them.
handles.charter: Daniel, 2026-10-13 (a new slice, in architecture's rollout)
examples: How much slower does serving a model get when you add verification, and how did you measure that?
What's the overhead of the bandwidth audit (or PoUW, or the commitment) compared with plain vLLM?
Can I rerun one of your benchmark numbers myself, and how?
Why do two of your overhead numbers for the same thing disagree?
How do you make sure a benchmark comparison is fair, with the same model, settings and GPU, and warm-ups excluded?

handles.remit: Fast commitment kernels: one GPU library for every served-path commitment, its vLLM integration, the commit-overhead benchmark.
handles.charter: Daniel, 2026-10-17 10:46 PM PDT (a new slice, via top); renamed from @hash by Daniel, 2026-10-18 9:40 AM PDT
examples: How much slower is serving with the commitments on, compared with plain vLLM at full load?
Why is the proof-of-work matmul so much slower than a normal int8 matmul, and what would make it faster?
Is the exact int8 path supposed to be slower than ordinary int8 serving?
How much GPU time does SHA-512 hashing take next to the model's own work?
How do you measure the overhead fairly: against which baseline, at what batch size, on which GPUs?

handles.remit: Training compute and scaling laws: Daniel's training agent, for scaling-law questions.
examples: How much more hardware would someone need to secretly train a frontier model under your verification scheme?
Could a lab hide training inside work it declares and proves as inference?
Which parts of the training-slowdown claim are proved, and which are still assumptions?
If a lab hides some of its GPUs from monitoring, how much protection is left?
What would have to improve for the slowdown to go from about 30x to over 1,000x?

handles.remit: The one soundness theorem: Verity.Soundness over the compiled verifier, every subprotocol it rests on, and their composition.
handles.charter: Daniel, 2026-10-26 10:04 AM PDT (pull the full proofs in; a new slice, via top, split from proofs at its worker cap)
examples: Is there one theorem that says the whole verifier is sound, and what does it still assume?
Which subprotocols of the soundness theorem are proved, and which are still premises?
If the verifier accepts a period, what exactly does that guarantee about the work, memory and network claims?
When will Verity.Soundness be on main with no subprotocol left as a hypothesis?
Does the theorem cover the code that actually runs, or a model of it?
